channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest Brussels posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: Morocco appoints first female head of government
item.description: Mansouri is also mayor of Marrakech.

item.title: Brussels appeal court asks for extra staff as cases delayed until 2028
item.description: More than 5,000 cases are waiting to be dealt with at the Brussels Court of Appeal, where a lack of judges and other staff means some cases will not be heard until September 2028.

item.title: Belgian government must address Brussels Airport noise concerns by Thursday
item.description: If the Belgian government does not meet certain requirements by Thursday, it will be fined €10,000 a day for up to 200 days.

item.title: International students contribute 'much more' to Belgian economy than they cost, study shows
item.description: As Belgium is looking to cut costs and crack down on migration, tuition fees for international students are skyrocketing.

item.title: Brussels business club owner on the radar for suspected Chinese interference
item.description: Western intelligence services have been on high alert in recent weeks, following two high-profile cases of Chinese espionage in Belgium this summer.

item.title: Brussels Parliament will not summon Public Prosecutor after political interference row
item.description: The Brussels Parliament decided not to summon public prosecutor Julien Moinil after he revealed he was contacted by an MP with a request to release a prisoner.

item.title: One unnamed MP, 89 under suspicion: Prosecutor's revelation rattles Brussels Parliament
item.description: Brussels parties want answers after Public Prosecutor Julien Moinil revealed that an unnamed MP asked him to release an inmate, placing suspicion on all 89 Brussels MPs.

item.title: Vlaams Belang to take Brussels hospitals' Dutch language issues to Council of Europe
item.description: “Year after year, government after government, Dutch-speakers are told that things will be sorted out. In practice, nothing changes at all."

item.title: Brussels' historic Grand-Place complex might get major revamp
item.description: The project, which would be carried out on one of the most iconic places in Brussels, is particularly sensitive.

item.title: How fear of homophobia changes the way queer people move through Brussels
item.description: Queer people in Brussels describe the everyday calculations they make to feel safe while moving through the city.

item.title: After cancer treatment, the hardest part can still be rebuilding a life
item.description: “The doctor prescribes you a treatment, they prescribe you a diagnosis, but you are unique in living the disease.”

item.title: Hundreds protest with empty plates in Brussels
item.description: Food aid groups warned the system is “unsustainable,” with longer queues, smaller parcels and a 134% rise in meals and food parcels distributed over six years.

item.title: 140 passengers stranded on Brussels Airlines flight in Sicily
item.description: An ash cloud from Mount Etna has forced airport closures, with flights rerouted via Palermo and at least one scheduled Sunday departure cancelled.

item.title: French-speakers' minister-president 'understands' anger after budget cuts
item.description: Elisabeth Degryse has reacted to the widespread backlash following the French community's recent budget cuts.

item.title: People collect over a ton of trash in Brussels on World Cleanup Week
item.description: 1,302 volunteers, including numerous schools and companies, took part in the event to help rid the Belgian capital of litter.

item.title: Over 5,000 attend Grand Rendez-Vous by Wallonia-Brussels Federation
item.description: The event featured cinema-related performances as part of a week-long festival.

item.title: Unwrapping the Palace of Justice: Can Brussels learn to love its troubled giant?
item.description: For more than 40 years, Brussels’ Palace of Justice was hidden behind scaffolding, a monument to neglect as much as to justice. Now its grand façade has finally re-emerged.

item.title: Empty European Commission offices might make way for housing and shops
item.description: Former European Commission offices in Auderghem could be transformed into 189 homes as Brussels adapts to falling demand for office space.

item.title: Seven suspects arrested in deadly nightshop robbery Ixelles
item.description: Belgian police have identified and arrested seven suspects for the murder of the owner of a night shop in Ixelles who died during a robbery in August.

item.title: What to do in Brussels this weekend: 25 – 27 September
item.description: Want to end September on a high note? Consider adding these events to your calendar.
